Consider the following statements related to Gandhara art forms other than stone sculpture:

Statement 1: A decorated gold reliquary featuring standing figures was unearthed at the Bimaran site.

Statement 2: Begram excavations revealed finely carved ivory panels used for decorative purposes.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gandhara art** is known for its synthesis of **Greco-Roman and Indian artistic styles**, primarily flourishing in the areas of modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• **Statement 1:** The decorated gold reliquary unearthed at the **Bimaran site** is a notable artifact associated with Gandhara art. It features **standing figures**, showcasing intricate craftsmanship and the influence of Greco-Roman artistic traditions.
 
• **Statement 2:** The excavations at **Begram** revealed finely carved ivory panels, which were used for **decorative purposes**. These panels reflect the high level of artistry and the cross-cultural influences present in Gandhara art.
 
• Both statements highlight the diversity of Gandhara art forms, extending beyond stone sculptures to include **metalwork and ivory carvings**.
 
• The discovery of such artifacts suggests the **rich cultural exchanges** and trade networks in the region during ancient times.
 
• Gandhara art predominantly thrived under the patronage of rulers like the **Kushans**, especially Emperor **Kanishka**.
 
• These artistic traditions played a significant role in the spread of **Buddhist art** and iconography across Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bimaran site**__

 __
 
• The **Bimaran site** is located in modern-day Afghanistan and is famous for the discovery of a gold reliquary.
 
• This reliquary is believed to be one of the earliest depictions of **Buddha in anthropomorphic form**.
 
• The artifact exemplifies the amalgamation of **Greco-Roman and Buddhist iconography**.
 
 
 
• **Begram excavations**__
 __
 
• **Begram**, near Kabul in Afghanistan, was a prominent trade center during ancient times.
 
• The excavations uncovered a wide range of artifacts, including **ivory carvings, glassware, and coins**, indicating its importance in ancient trade networks.
 
• The finely carved ivory panels are believed to have been used as furniture decorations or for other ornamental purposes.
 
 
 
• **Kushan patronage**__
 
 
• The **Kushan Empire** was instrumental in the development and spread of Gandhara art.
 
• Under rulers like Emperor **Kanishka**, Gandhara art flourished, blending **local Indian traditions with Greco-Roman artistic styles**.
 
• The empire promoted Buddhist art and culture, leading to the creation of iconic artifacts and sculptures.

questions.question: Which option best captures the cultural importance of the Kanuma festival celebrated in Andhra Pradesh?

options.text: Observance linked to forest conservation rituals
Festival devoted to worshipping agricultural cattle
Celebration marking the end of winter solstice

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Festival devoted to worshipping agricultural cattle**__.

__
 
• **Kanuma** festival is an important part of the celebrations during the **Sankranti festival** in **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It is a day specifically devoted to **worshipping agricultural cattle**, such as cows, bulls, and oxen.
 
• The festival signifies the critical role of cattle in **agriculture and rural livelihoods**.
 
• Farmers and rural communities express their gratitude to cattle, acknowledging their contribution to **ploughing fields** and other agricultural activities.
 
• On Kanuma, cattle are cleaned, decorated with **flowers and turmeric**, and sometimes painted with natural colors as a sign of celebration.
 
• Special rituals and offerings are made to honor the cattle, reflecting the importance of **traditional agrarian practices**.
 
• Kanuma is part of the larger Sankranti celebrations, which include **Pongal and Bhogi**, focusing on themes of **harvest, gratitude, and renewal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Observance linked to forest conservation rituals**__

 __
 
• Forest conservation rituals typically focus on **preserving biodiversity** and ensuring the sustainable use of forest resources.
 
• These types of rituals are observed in various parts of India but are not a central theme of the **Kanuma festival**.
 
 
 
• **Event commemorating river goddesses**__
 __
 
• The worship of river goddesses is common in India, especially in festivals dedicated to sacred rivers such as the **Ganga, Yamuna, or Narmada**.
 
• While such rituals are significant, they are not related to the **Kanuma festival**, which is focused on cattle worship.
 
 
 
• **Celebration marking the end of winter solstice**__
 
 
• The winter solstice is associated with various festivals globally, often signifying the **return of longer days**.
 
• In India, the Sankranti festival as a whole marks the **transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara)**, but Kanuma specifically focuses on cattle worship.

Consider the following statements regarding World Championship swimming events conducted in a 50-metre pool:

Statement 1: Freestyle events for men and women include races from 50 metres up to 1500 metres.

Statement 2: Individual Medley events are conducted only up to a maximum distance of 400 metres.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **World Championship swimming events**, freestyle races for both men and women include events ranging from **50 metres to 1500 metres**. These distances are standard across international competitions held in **50-metre pools**, also known as Olympic-sized pools.
 
• The Individual Medley (IM) is a swimming event where a single swimmer uses all four strokes—**butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle**—in a set sequence. These events are conducted up to a **maximum distance of 400 metres** in World Championship swimming events.
 
• The statement regarding freestyle events is correct as they cover distances of **50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, and 1500m**.
 
• The statement about Individual Medley is also correct because the **400m Individual Medley** is the longest IM event conducted in international competitions. There is no IM event beyond this distance.
 
• These swimming events are governed by the **International Swimming Federation (FINA)**, the world body that sets rules and regulations for swimming competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Freestyle Events**__

 __
 
• The **freestyle stroke** is the fastest and most common stroke used in competitive swimming.
 
• Freestyle events include distances of **50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, and 1500m**. The **800m freestyle** is a recent addition for men in major competitions.
 
• Freestyle events allow swimmers to choose any stroke; however, the front crawl is almost exclusively used because of its efficiency and speed.
 
 
 
• **Individual Medley**__
 
 
• The **Individual Medley (IM)** requires swimmers to swim equal distances of four strokes in the following order: **butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle.**
 
• IM events are held over **200m and 400m** distances in international competitions.
 
• The 400m IM is considered one of the most challenging events as it tests the swimmer's versatility and endurance across all four strokes.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Random mixture of sediments deposited by ice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glacial till** is an unsorted material deposited directly by glacier ice without the intervention of meltwater streams.
 
• It is characterized by a **random mixture of sediments** that include clay, silt, sand, gravel, and boulders, which are not sorted or layered.
 
• Unlike sediments transported by meltwater streams, glacial till lacks **visible stratification or sorting** due to the direct deposition by ice.
 
• This type of deposition occurs when the glacier melts and drops its load of debris, resulting in a **heterogeneous mixture** of materials.
 
• Because the sediments are transported by solid ice, they can be angular or subangular in shape, unlike the smoother, rounded sediments transported by water.
 
• Glacial till can cover large areas and often forms landforms such as **moraines** and **drumlins**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Presence of visible layering**__

 __
 
• Layering is a characteristic of sediments deposited by **meltwater streams** or other water bodies, not glacial till.
 
• Such sediments are often **stratified** and show clear layers due to the settling of particles based on size and weight in flowing water.
 
• This is not applicable to glacial till as it forms through direct deposition by ice.
 
 
 
• **Uniform grain size**__
 __
 
• Uniform grain size is a feature of well-sorted sediments, often found in riverbeds or wind-deposited materials like dunes.
 
• Glacial till, however, is **unsorted** and contains a mix of grain sizes, ranging from fine clay to large boulders.
 
 
 
• **Formation only in glacial lakes**__
 
 
• This is not correct, as glacial till forms directly under or in front of a glacier, not exclusively in glacial lakes.
 
• While glacial lakes do receive sediments, these are typically sorted due to the action of water, unlike the unsorted nature of glacial till.

Evaluate the following statements related to satellite orbits:

Statement 1: Sun-synchronous orbits allow satellites to pass over a location at nearly the same local solar time.

Statement 2: Such orbits are typically used for communication satellites placed in geostationary orbit.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Sun-synchronous orbits are designed to ensure that the satellite passes over a specific location on Earth at approximately the same local solar time. This consistency is critical for applications such as **Earth observation** and **remote sensing**, where uniform lighting conditions are essential for accurate data collection.
 
• The inclination angle of a Sun-synchronous orbit is carefully chosen so that the orbit precesses at the same rate as the Earth's rotation around the Sun. This allows satellites to maintain the same angle with respect to the Sun.
 
• Satellites in Sun-synchronous orbits are typically used for purposes such as **weather monitoring**, **climate studies**, **environmental observations**, and **mapping**.
 
• **Statement 2:** This is incorrect because **communication satellites** are not typically placed in Sun-synchronous orbits. Instead, they are usually deployed in **geostationary orbits** to provide continuous coverage of a particular area on Earth's surface. Such satellites remain fixed relative to a point on Earth, making them ideal for communication purposes.
 
• Geostationary orbits are at an altitude of approximately **35,786 km** above the equator and revolve around Earth at the same rotational speed as the planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Applications of Sun-Synchronous Orbits:**__

 __
 
• Primarily used in **Earth observation** and **remote sensing satellites**.
 
• Examples include satellites like **Sentinel-2** and **Landsat**, which monitor environmental changes, deforestation, urbanization, and climate patterns.
 
• They provide images and data under consistent lighting conditions, enabling accurate comparisons over time.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Geostationary Orbits:**__
 
 
• Used extensively for **telecommunication**, **TV broadcasting**, and **weather monitoring satellites**.
 
• Examples include **INSAT** and **GOES satellites**, which deliver real-time data for weather forecasting and disaster management.
 
• Due to their fixed position relative to Earth, they offer uninterrupted coverage of specific areas.

questions.question: Which part of the human brain plays a key role in regulating circadian rhythm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypothalamus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **hypothalamus** is a small region located at the base of the brain, near the pituitary gland.
 
• It plays a crucial role in regulating the **circadian rhythm**, which is the body's internal biological clock that governs the sleep-wake cycle and other physiological processes.
 
• The specific part of the hypothalamus involved in circadian rhythm regulation is the **suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)**.
 
• The SCN receives signals about light and darkness from the retina in the eyes via the **retinohypothalamic tract**.
 
• Based on light exposure, the SCN sends signals to regulate the production of **melatonin**, a hormone secreted by the pineal gland that influences sleep patterns.
 
• The hypothalamus is also involved in controlling other vital functions such as **body temperature, hunger, thirst, and emotional responses.**
 
• Disruption in the hypothalamus or the SCN can lead to **sleep disorders**, jet lag, or other circadian-related issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cerebellum**__

 __
 
• The **cerebellum** is located at the back of the brain, below the occipital lobes and behind the brainstem.
 
• It is primarily responsible for **coordinating voluntary movements**, maintaining balance, posture, and motor learning.
 
• The cerebellum does not regulate circadian rhythms but is crucial for motor control and precision.
 
 
 
• **Pons**__
 __
 
• The **pons** is part of the brainstem and serves as a bridge between different parts of the nervous system, including the cerebrum and cerebellum.
 
• It is involved in functions such as **facial expressions, breathing, and sleep regulation**, but it does not directly control circadian rhythms.
 
 
 
• **Thalamus**__
 
 
• The **thalamus** is located above the hypothalamus and acts as a **relay center** for sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex.
 
• While it plays a role in sensory perception and regulation of consciousness, it is not directly involved in circadian rhythm regulation.

Consider the following statements regarding collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers:

Statement 1: The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Statement 2: In bicameral states, the State Council of Ministers is responsible to the Legislative Council.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only Statement 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Indian Constitution, the **Union Council of Ministers** is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**, which is the **lower house** of Parliament.
 
• This principle of collective responsibility is enshrined in **Article 75(3)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• It means that all ministers stand and fall together; if the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, all ministers must resign.
 
• The concept of collective responsibility ensures a unified approach in decision-making by the Council of Ministers.
 
• It is a key feature of the **parliamentary system** of government as practiced in India.
 
• Statement 1 is correct because it aligns with the constitutional provision that the Union Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement 2: In bicameral states, the State Council of Ministers is responsible to the Legislative Council**__

 
 
• This statement is incorrect because, in states with a bicameral legislature, the **State Council of Ministers** is responsible to the **Legislative Assembly**, which is the **lower house**, and not the Legislative Council.
 
• This principle is outlined in **Article 164(2)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Legislative Council (upper house) does not hold the State Council of Ministers collectively accountable.
 
• In states, the Legislative Assembly plays a role similar to the Lok Sabha at the Union level in ensuring accountability of the executive.

Consider the following statements regarding the office of the Governor:

Statement 1: Article 356(1) refers to the Governor’s report recommending President’s Rule.

Statement 2: The Sarkaria Commission advised restraint in removing Governors before completion of their term.

Statement 3: The 41st Constitutional Amendment reduced the Governor’s tenure to four years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Statement 1 and Statement 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 356(1)** of the Indian Constitution refers to the Governor’s report recommending **President’s Rule** in a state in case of the failure of constitutional machinery.
 
• The Governor is responsible for sending such a report to the President when the governance in a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission**, constituted in 1983 to review Centre-State relations, advised **restraint in the arbitrary removal of Governors** before the completion of their tenure. This was to ensure the independence and impartiality of the office of the Governor.
 
• The **41st Constitutional Amendment**, as mentioned in the statement, does not exist. Hence, the claim about reducing the Governor's tenure to four years is incorrect.
 
• The tenure of the Governor, as per the Constitution, is still fixed at **five years**, though they hold office during the pleasure of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Incorrect Statement: The 41st Constitutional Amendment reduced the Governor's tenure to four years**__

 
 
• The **41st Constitutional Amendment** does not relate to the Governor's tenure. It is a misinterpretation.
 
• The **Governor's tenure** is prescribed as **five years** under Article 156 of the Constitution, but they hold office at the **pleasure of the President**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points related to the Governor’s Office:**
 
 
• The Governor is the **constitutional head of the state** and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Article 356, which allows for the imposition of **President’s Rule**, is based on the report submitted by the Governor.
 
• Recommendations of the **Sarkaria Commission** emphasize the Governor's independence and neutrality to maintain the federal structure.

questions.question: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is approximately:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**25 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **least distance of distinct vision** is the minimum distance at which the eye can clearly focus an object.
 
• For a normal human eye, this distance is approximately **25 cm**.
 
• This is the distance at which the eye's **lens system** can focus an object on the retina without strain.
 
• This value can vary depending on the individual’s **age** and condition of their eyes, such as in cases of **myopia** or **hypermetropia**.
 
• The value of 25 cm is used as a standard in **optics calculations** and for designing optical instruments like microscopes and magnifying glasses.
 
• At this distance, the eye experiences **minimal strain** while observing an object for a long time.
 
• This is a critical parameter in understanding the functioning of the **human eye** and is often used in physics and biology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **2.5 cm**__

 __
 
• A distance of **2.5 cm** is too short for the human eye to focus clearly. Objects at this distance cause excessive strain and appear blurry for a normal eye.
 
 
 
• **2.5 m**__
 __
 
• A distance of **2.5 m** is far beyond the least distance of distinct vision. Objects at this range can still be seen clearly but don’t represent the minimum distance.
 
 
 
• **25 m**__
 
 
• At **25 m**, the eye focuses easily, but this distance is far greater than the closest point of distinct vision.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, what is the maximum detention period before default bail for offences punishable with less than 10 years?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**60 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023** replaces the colonial-era criminal procedure laws in India to modernize and streamline the judicial processes.
 
• Under the provisions of the **BNSS, 2023**, the maximum detention period before granting default bail for offences punishable with imprisonment of less than 10 years is set to **60 days**.
 
• This provision aims to ensure a balance between the investigation of offences and the rights of accused individuals to not face indefinite incarceration without trial.
 
• The concept of **default bail** is rooted in the protection of personal liberty as enshrined under **Article 21 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• If the investigation is not completed within the prescribed period (in this case, **60 days**), the accused becomes entitled to bail as a matter of right.
 
• The **BNSS, 2023** aligns with India’s commitment to protecting human rights while maintaining justice and order.
 
• This provision is part of the reformatory changes aimed at reducing delays and increasing efficiency in the criminal justice system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **15 days**__

 __
 
• The detention period of **15 days** is typically applicable in cases of minor offences or for initial custody orders under certain laws.
 
• This duration is not sufficient for complex investigations involving offences punishable with imprisonment of less than 10 years, as defined in the **BNSS, 2023**.
 
 
 
• **30 days**__
 __
 
• A detention period of **30 days** may apply to cases requiring shorter investigatory timelines, but it is not the maximum limit under the given provisions of **BNSS, 2023**.
 
 
 
• **90 days**__
 
 
• The detention period of **90 days** is applicable for serious offences where the punishment is imprisonment of 10 years or more, as per the **BNSS, 2023**.
 
• This provision ensures that adequate time is given to the investigation of grave offences like murder or terrorism-related activities.

questions.question: Poikkal Kuthirai Aattam, also known as the dummy horse dance, is traditionally associated with which state?

The Correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poikkal Kuthirai Aattam**, also known as the **dummy horse dance**, is a traditional folk dance form performed in **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• The term "Poikkal Kuthirai" translates to **"false leg horse"**, as performers use a dummy horse attached to their waists to create an illusion of riding a horse.
 
• This dance is performed during **festivals, temple ceremonies, and cultural events** as part of Tamil Nadu's vibrant folk traditions.
 
• The dummy horse used in the dance is beautifully decorated with **colorful fabrics, ornaments, and intricate designs** to enhance the visual appeal.
 
• Performers showcase their **artistic skills** by synchronizing their movements with rhythmic music played on traditional instruments like the **nadaswaram and thavil.**
 
• The dance is not just entertaining but also represents the **rich cultural heritage and folklore** of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Poikkal Kuthirai Aattam is often performed to honor **deities** and express devotion during religious events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kerala**__

 __
 
• **Kerala** is known for its traditional dance forms such as **Kathakali**, which is a classical dance-drama, and **Mohiniyattam**, a graceful semi-classical dance.
 
• Kerala's folk traditions include **Theyyam**, a ritualistic dance form performed in temples.
 
• The state is famous for its rich cultural heritage, which reflects in its diverse dance and music traditions.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__
 __
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** is known for its classical dance form **Kuchipudi**, which originated in the village of the same name in the state.
 
• The state also has various folk dances such as **Veeranatyam**, a dance performed in honor of Lord Shiva.

• **Karnataka**__
 
 
• **Karnataka** is famous for classical dance forms such as **Bharatanatyam** and folk dances like **Yakshagana**, a traditional theater art.
 
• Yakshagana combines dance, music, and drama to depict stories from Indian mythology.
 
• Karnataka is also known for unique folk performances such as **Dollu Kunitha**, a drum dance performed by men.

questions.question: What does a lower value on the Corruption Perceptions Index indicate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Higher corruption levels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is a widely used indicator released by **Transparency International**, which measures the perceived levels of public sector corruption in different countries worldwide.
 
• A **lower score** on the index indicates **higher corruption levels** in the country’s public sector, reflecting poor governance, lack of transparency, and weak institutions.
 
• The index ranks countries on a scale from **0 (highly corrupt)** to **100 (very clean)**.
 
• The CPI is based on expert assessments and surveys of businesspeople, which analyze corruption in areas such as **bribery, misuse of public funds, and lack of integrity in public office.**
 
• Countries with **lower scores** often face challenges such as **weak rule of law, minimal accountability, and inefficient public services**, all of which contribute to higher corruption levels.
 
• The index is a valuable tool for global organizations, policymakers, and governments to assess and address corruption issues in their respective regions.
 
• Examples of countries with lower CPI scores are often those experiencing **political instability, economic challenges, and weak regulatory frameworks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Improved governance**__

 __
 
• **Improved governance** is associated with higher scores on the CPI, as it reflects enhanced transparency, accountability, and a reduction in corruption levels.
 
• Countries with improved governance demonstrate **strong institutions** and efficient public sector management.
 
 
 
• **Strong transparency**__
 __
 
• **Strong transparency** is a characteristic of nations with high CPI scores, as it reflects openness and honesty in government dealings.
 
• Transparency ensures **public access to information** and reduces the opportunities for corruption.
 
 
 
• **Effective institutions**__
 
 
• Countries with **effective institutions** ensure the proper functioning of public offices and effective delivery of services, which generally lead to higher CPI scores.
 
• Such institutions promote the **rule of law, accountability, and integrity** in governance.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents agro-based industries?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cotton textiles and sugar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agro-based industries** refer to industries that depend on agricultural raw materials for their production.
 
• **Cotton textiles** are a significant agro-based industry as they rely on **cotton**, a major agricultural crop, for manufacturing fabric and clothing.
 
• **Sugar** production is another agro-based industry, as it uses **sugarcane**, a vital agricultural product, as its raw material.
 
• Both industries contribute significantly to the **economy**, providing employment and boosting agricultural activities.
 
• These industries are widely prevalent in regions with high agricultural output, such as **Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat**.
 
• Agro-based industries play a crucial role in ensuring sustainable utilization of **agricultural resources**.
 
• They help in strengthening the **rural economy** by creating jobs for people in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cement and fertilisers**__

 __
 
• **Cement** is a mineral-based industry that uses raw materials like limestone, clay, and gypsum, making it unrelated to agriculture.
 
• **Fertilisers** are chemical-based products that enhance agricultural productivity, but they are not directly derived from agricultural products.
 
 
 
• **Steel and machinery**__
 __
 
• **Steel** and **machinery industries** are mineral and engineering-based industries that use metals like iron and steel, which are mined rather than grown.
 
• They do not depend on agricultural products.
 
 
 
• **Aluminium and petroleum**__

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was removed by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Constitutional Amendment Act**, enacted in **1978**, removed the **Right to Property** as a Fundamental Right.
 
• Earlier, the Right to Property was provided under **Article 31** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment demoted the Right to Property to a **legal right** under **Article 300A** of the Constitution.
 
• The rationale for this change was to ensure **social justice** and to prevent the misuse of property rights to hinder the implementation of land reforms.
 
• Under **Article 300A**, no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• The removal of the Right to Property allowed the government to acquire private property for public purposes without being restricted by Fundamental Rights.
 
• The amendment was introduced by the **Janata Party** government led by **Prime Minister Morarji Desai**.
 
• This change made India one of the few countries where the Right to Property is not a Fundamental Right.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Equality**__

 __
 
• The **Right to Equality** is provided under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It ensures equality before the law, prohibits discrimination on various grounds, and abolishes untouchability and titles.
 
• This right is a cornerstone for ensuring social justice and equality in India.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom**__
 __
 
• The **Right to Freedom** is provided under **Articles 19 to 22** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It includes rights such as freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• This right ensures personal liberty and safeguards against arbitrary actions by the state.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation**__
 
 
• The **Right against Exploitation** is provided under **Articles 23 and 24** of the Constitution.
 
• It prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and employment of children below 14 years in hazardous industries.
 
• This right upholds human dignity and protects vulnerable sections of society from exploitation.

• India is often described as a **quasi-federal state** due to its unique federal structure that shows a bias toward the **Union Government**.

• Key provisions such as the **Union List** in the Seventh Schedule emphasize the predominance of the Union Government in legislative matters.

• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct speech: "He said"
 
• Remains the same in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**

• The sentence is reported with correct tense and time expression adjustments.
